decision.observed_event: You want in. Two ways to play a round: settle it with one check, or play it out as twenty-one (blackjack), closest to 21 without going over. The stake is your 12 gp. Which way?

appraisal.label: frustration
appraisal.cause: The rogue tries to show the deck.

improv_read.player_bid: Wren spreads the deck to show the backs.
improv_read.connection: Uktarl reroutes trouble into the game.
improv_read.kit_choice: Kit lets the dealer bulldoze past the reveal, following the table state.

public_brief.objective: Smother the accusation by getting her playing.
public_brief.tactic: Sweep the cards up and push the game at a higher stake.
public_brief.visible_cue: He gathers the spread deck back into a block with one sweep.
public_brief.player_opening: She can play by hand or check, or keep pressing the accusation.
public_brief.reply_to: I flip the deck face-down and show everyone the marks on the backs.
public_brief.kit_focus: Keep it to his hands sweeping the evidence away and the new offer.
public_brief.mirror: steady energy, standard, dry humor: the dealer answers with smooth evasion

segments.speaker: Narrator
segments.text: She turns the deck over and spreads the backs across the wood. The dealer watches her do it with polite patience, then gathers the cards back into one neat block with a single sweep of his palm.

segments.speaker: Dealer
segments.text: Thorough, madam, thorough. If you are so eager to study my cards, perhaps you should simply play them. Twelve gold, then, since you have such an appetite: card by card, or one throw of fortune and done with it?

segments.speaker: Kit
segments.text: He wants twelve gold now. Card by card, or one check?
segments.reacts_to: card by card, or one throw of fortune
